s0201.literal: Andu, Zhou Wenyu, and Xu Jingcheng were alike imprisoned by Lin.
s0201.idiomatic: Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyu, and Xu Jingcheng were all imprisoned by Wang Lin.

s0202.literal: Lin always bound them with one long chain and placed them under the boat shelter, ordering his close eunuch Wang Zijin to supervise them.
s0202.idiomatic: Lin always bound them with one long chain and kept them under the boats, putting his trusted eunuch Wang Zijin in charge of watching them.

s0203.literal: When Lin descended to White Water Ford at Pencheng, Andu and the rest with sweet words promised Zijin great bribes.
s0203.idiomatic: When Lin went down to White Water Ford at Pencheng, Andu and the others flattered Zijin and promised him rich bribes.

s0204.literal: Zijin then feigned fishing in a small boat by the shelter; at night he carried Andu, Wenyu, and Jingcheng ashore into deep grass, and on foot they fled to the government army.
s0204.idiomatic: Zijin then pretended to fish from a small boat moored by the shelter; at night he ferried Andu, Wenyu, and Jingcheng ashore into deep grass, and they made their way on foot to the imperial army.

s0205.literal: Returning to the capital he impeached himself; an edict specially pardoned him and restored his office and rank.
s0205.idiomatic: Back in the capital he submitted a confession; an edict granted him special pardon and restored his offices and titles.

s0206.literal: Soon he was made Intendant of Danyang, then sent out as Director-General of all military affairs in Southern Yuzhou, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
s0206.idiomatic: Soon he became intendant of Danyang, then was sent out as director-general of all military affairs in Southern Yuzhou, general who pacifies the west, and Southern Yuzhou inspector.

s0207.literal: He was ordered to follow Zhou Wenyu in attacking Yu Xiaomo and Wang Lin's generals Cao Qing, Chang Hong'ai, and others.
s0207.idiomatic: He was ordered to follow Zhou Wenyu against Yu Xiaomo and Wang Lin's generals Cao Qing, Chang Hong'ai, and others.

s0208.literal: Andu left from Gongting Lake through Song Gate and tracked Hong'ai's rear.
s0208.idiomatic: Andu left Gongting Lake by Song Gate and pressed on Hong'ai's rear.

s0209.literal: Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang; Andu turned back to take great ships and happened on Lin's generals Zhou Jiong and Zhou Xie returning south; he fought, defeated them, and captured Jiong and Xie alive.
s0209.idiomatic: Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang; Andu turned back for large ships, met Lin's generals Zhou Jiong and Zhou Xie heading south, defeated them, and took Jiong and Xie alive.

s0210.literal: Xiaomo's younger brother Xiaoyou led four thousand households of his following intending to join Wang Lin; encountering Jiong and Xie's defeat, he thereupon came to Andu and surrendered.
s0210.idiomatic: Xiaomo's brother Xiaoyou led four thousand households toward Wang Lin; when Jiong and Xie were beaten, he came to Andu and surrendered.

s0211.literal: Andu again advanced to Qinqi Isle, defeated Cao Qing, Chang Hong'ai, and the rest, and burned their ships.
s0211.idiomatic: Andu advanced again to Qinqi Isle, routed Cao Qing, Chang Hong'ai, and the rest, and burned their fleet.

s0212.literal: Hong'ai fled to Mount Lu and was killed by villagers; the remaining Hong factions were all pacified.
s0212.idiomatic: Hong'ai fled to Mount Lu, where villagers killed him; the rest of the Hong faction was pacified.

s0213.literal: Returning the army to Southern Wan, the Founder died; Andu followed Emperor Wen back to court and still joined the great ministers in settling plans to aid and install Emperor Wen.
s0213.idiomatic: On the march back to Southern Wan the Founder died; Andu followed Emperor Wen to court and joined the great ministers in settling the succession and supporting him.

s0214.literal: At the time Emperor Wen modestly declined and dared not accept; the empress dowager also because of the Prince of Hengyang would not issue the order; the great ministers hesitated and could not decide.
s0214.idiomatic: Emperor Wen modestly refused the throne; the empress dowager, mindful of the Prince of Hengyang, would not issue the order; the ministers wavered and could not decide.

s0215.literal: Andu said: "Now the four directions are unsettled—who has leisure for distant concerns? The Prince of Linchuan has merit under heaven; we must together install him.
s0215.idiomatic: Andu said: "The realm is still unsettled—who has time for distant claims? The Prince of Linchuan has served the realm; we must enthrone him together.

s0216.literal: In today's matter, whoever responds afterward is to be beheaded."
s0216.idiomatic: Whoever hesitates today will be beheaded."

s0217.literal: He then pressed up to the hall, told the empress dowager to bring out the seal, and with his own hands loosened Emperor Wen's hair and pushed him toward the mourning place.
s0217.idiomatic: He then escorted him into the hall, had the empress dowager produce the seal, loosened Emperor Wen's mourning hair with his own hands, and pushed him to the mourning hall.

s0218.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, [Andu] was transferred to Minister of Works and still made Director-General of all military affairs in Southern Xuzhou, General Who Campaigns North, and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, with staff of honor.
s0218.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Andu was made minister of works and still director-general of all military affairs in Southern Xuzhou, general who campaigns north, and Southern Xuzhou inspector, with an honorary staff.

s0219.literal: He still separately received a secret imperial order to welcome Xian, Prince of Hengyang, Chang.
s0219.idiomatic: He also received a separate secret order to welcome Xian, Prince of Hengyang, Chang.

s0220.literal: Initially, when Chang was about to enter, he sent a letter to Emperor Wen with language very lacking in deference; Emperor Wen was displeased and thus summoned Andu to speak at ease, saying: "The crown prince is about to arrive; we must seek another fief elsewhere—I am getting old."
s0220.idiomatic: When Chang was about to return, he wrote to Emperor Wen in very insolent terms; the emperor was displeased and summoned Andu to speak privately: "The crown prince is coming; I must find another domain to retire to—I am growing old."

s0221.literal: Andu replied: "Since antiquity has there ever been a Son of Heaven who was replaced?
s0221.idiomatic: Andu answered: "Has there ever been a Son of Heaven who was replaced?

s0222.literal: Your servant is dull and dares not receive such an order."
s0222.idiomatic: Your servant is too dull to obey such an order."

s0223.literal: He thereupon asked to go himself to welcome Chang; Chang crossed the Han and died.
s0223.idiomatic: He asked to go welcome Chang himself; Chang crossed the Han and died on the way.

s0224.literal: For merit he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qingyuan commandery, fief four thousand households.
s0224.idiomatic: For merit he was advanced to duke of Qingyuan commandery with a fief of four thousand households.

s0225.literal: From this his martial fame was very heavy; among the great ministers none exceeded him.
s0225.idiomatic: From then on his prestige was immense; no minister outranked him.

s0226.literal: Andu's father Wenhan was Administrator of Shixing interior; he died in office.
s0226.idiomatic: Andu's father Wenhan was administrator of Shixing interior and died in office.

s0227.literal: Emperor Wen summoned Andu back to the capital to hold mourning.
s0227.idiomatic: Emperor Wen recalled Andu to the capital to observe mourning.

s0228.literal: Soon he was recalled to his former office; his father was posthumously given Gentleman at the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Master of the Household with the Golden Sigil and Purple Tassel; his mother was invested as Grand Lady of Qingyuan state.
s0228.idiomatic: He soon returned to his former post; his father was posthumously made gentleman at the imperial secretariat and grand master of the household with the golden sigil and purple tassel; his mother was made grand lady of Qingyuan state.

s0229.literal: He still welcomed [her] back to the capital; his mother firmly asked to remain in the countryside; the sovereign then issued an edict, changing Guiyang's Rucheng county into
s0229.idiomatic: He still brought her toward the capital; his mother insisted on staying in her home district; the court then decreed that Rucheng county in Guiyang be made

s0231.literal: [Lu]yang commandery, [17] dividing Hengzhou's Shixing and Anyuan two commanderies, combining three commanderies into Eastern Hengzhou, with Andu's younger cousin Xiao as inspector; Andu's third son Mi at nine years of age the sovereign made Administrator of Shixing interior, and ordered both to remain in the countryside to attend and support [her].
s0231.idiomatic: [Lu]yang commandery, [17] taking Shixing and Anyuan from Hengzhou and combining three commanderies into Eastern Hengzhou with Andu's cousin Xiao as inspector; Andu's third son Mi, nine years old, was made administrator of Shixing interior, and both were ordered to stay home and serve her.

s0232.literal: That year, [Andu's] enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Guiyang commandery.
s0232.idiomatic: That year Andu's title was changed to duke of Guiyang commandery.

s0233.literal: After Wang Lin's defeat, Zhou armies entered and held Ba and Xiang; Andu received orders for a western campaign.
s0233.idiomatic: After Wang Lin's defeat Northern Zhou troops held Ba and Xiang; Andu was ordered west against them.

s0234.literal: When Liu Yi held Dongyang in rebellion, he again received orders for an eastern campaign.
s0234.idiomatic: When Liu Yi rebelled and held Dongyang, he was ordered east again.

s0235.literal: Yi had expected the court army to come up the Qiantang River; Andu instead marched overland through Zhuji in Kuaiji and emerged at Yongkang.
s0235.idiomatic: Yi expected the imperial army up the Qiantang; Andu marched overland through Zhuji in Kuaiji and came out at Yongkang.

s0236.literal: Yi was greatly afraid, fled to Taozhi Ridge, and lodged in a mountain ravine; at the mouth of the gorge he set palisades to resist the royal army.
s0236.idiomatic: Yi was terrified, fled to Taozhi Ridge, and camped in the ravines; at the pass he built palisades against the imperial force.

s0239.literal: [to attack] Yi, [18] personally joining battle; he was struck by a stray arrow and blood ran to his ankles; Andu rode in a litter to command the army, his bearing unchanged.
s0239.idiomatic: [to attack] Yi, [18] fighting in person; a stray arrow struck him and blood ran to his ankles; Andu directed the army from a litter without changing countenance.

s0240.literal: Using the steep mountain terrain, he dammed and penned the waters.
s0240.idiomatic: Using the steep mountain terrain, he dammed the stream.

s0241.literal: In summer of the third year of Tianjia, floods filled the dam; Andu brought boats into the barrier, raised tower ships level with Yi's wall, and smashed his parapets with rams.
s0241.idiomatic: In summer of Tianjia year 3 the dam filled; Andu brought ships in, raised tower ships level with Yi's wall, and smashed the parapets with rams.

s0242.literal: Yi and his second son Zhongchen escaped to Jin'an; Andu captured his wife and children, seized all his men, horses, armor, and weapons, and returned in triumph.
s0242.idiomatic: Yi and his second son Zhongchen fled to Jin'an; Andu took their families, seized men, horses, arms, and armor, and marched home in triumph.

s0243.literal: For merit he was given Palace Attendant and General Who Campaigns North, his fief increased by the former five thousand households, and he returned to his original command.
s0243.idiomatic: For merit he was made palace attendant and general who campaigns north, his fief was increased by five thousand households in all, and he returned to his former post.

s0246.literal: [Officials] and people came to court with a memorial requesting a stele, [19] praising Andu's achievements; the edict approved it.
s0246.idiomatic: [Officials] and commoners petitioned the throne for a stele, [19] praising Andu's deeds; the court assented.

s0247.literal: After Wang Lin was pacified, Andu's achievements grew ever greater; he also considered his merit had settled the altars, and gradually grew proud and arrogant, repeatedly gathering civil and military men—some to shoot, drive, and race, others ordered to compose poetry; he ranked them high and low and rewarded them in order.
s0247.idiomatic: After Wang Lin's fall Andu's merit grew; thinking he had secured the throne, he grew proud, gathered scholars and soldiers—some for archery and racing, others for verse—and ranked them for graded rewards.

s0250.literal: [Jie], [20] Ma Shu, Yin Keng, Zhang Zhengjian, Xu Boyang, Liu Shan, [21] Zu Sun Deng; among warriors Xiao Mohe, Pei Zilie, and others—all became his retainers, and within his residence there were often as many as a thousand.
s0250.idiomatic: [Jie], [20] Ma Shu, Yin Keng, Zhang Zhengjian, Xu Boyang, Liu Shan, [21] and Zu Sun Deng; among warriors Xiao Mohe, Pei Zilie, and others—all were his guests, and his household often held a thousand men.

s0251.literal: His subordinate commanders often did not obey the law; when investigated and arrested, they fled back to Andu.
s0251.idiomatic: His officers often broke the law; when the authorities investigated, they fled to Andu.

s0252.literal: Emperor Wen was by nature strict and observant and deeply resented this.
s0252.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was strict by nature and deeply resented it.

s0253.literal: Andu did not reform; day by day he grew more arrogant.
s0253.idiomatic: Andu did not change and grew daily more overbearing.

s0254.literal: Whenever he had a memorial, after sealing it, if something remained unsaid, he would open the seal and write himself, saying he also memorialized on such-and-such a matter.
s0254.idiomatic: When he sealed a memorial but still had more to say, he opened the seal and added lines himself, noting another petition on such-and-such.

s0255.literal: When attending banquets and drunk, he would sit with legs sprawled or lean recklessly.
s0255.idiomatic: At court feasts, drunk, he would sit sprawled or lean disrespectfully.

s0256.literal: Once at the Music Garden spring purification feast he said to the emperor: "How does this compare with being Prince of Linchuan?"
s0256.idiomatic: Once at the Music Garden spring rites he asked the emperor: "How is this compared with your days as Prince of Linchuan?"

s0258.literal: Andu spoke of it again and again; the emperor said: "Though this is heaven's mandate, it is also your lordship's strength."
s0258.idiomatic: Andu pressed the point; the emperor said: "Though heaven willed it, it was also your excellence."

s0259.literal: When the feast ended he again memorialized to borrow furnishings and aquatic decorations, intending to bring his wives and concubines to revel in the imperial hall; Emperor Wen though he granted the request was very displeased.
s0259.idiomatic: After the feast he asked to borrow hangings and water ornaments to bring his wives to feast in the imperial hall; Emperor Wen consented but was deeply displeased.

s0260.literal: The next day Andu sat on the imperial seat while his guests occupied the ministers' places, raising cups to offer longevity.
s0260.idiomatic: Next day Andu sat on the throne while guests took the ministers' seats and toasted the emperor.

s0261.literal: Earlier, when Chongyun Hall burned, Andu led armored soldiers into the hall; the emperor greatly detested this and from then secretly made preparations against him.
s0261.idiomatic: When Chongyun Hall burned, Andu had led armored troops inside; the emperor hated it and thereafter quietly prepared against him.

s0262.literal: Again when Zhou Di rebelled, the court expected Andu to be sent against him; the emperor instead sent Wu Mingche, and repeatedly dispatched court envoys to investigate Andu's subordinates and search out deserters; Andu was inwardly uneasy.
s0262.idiomatic: When Zhou Di rebelled the court had expected Andu to suppress him; the emperor sent Wu Mingche instead and repeatedly sent envoys to probe Andu's men and hunt deserters; Andu grew uneasy.

s0263.literal: In winter of the third year he sent his aide Zhou Hongshi to entrust himself to Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Jingli, presenting gifts and inquiring into affairs within the palace.
s0263.idiomatic: In winter of year 3 he sent aide Zhou Hongshi to attendant Cai Jingli with gifts, asking about palace affairs.

s0264.literal: Jingli recorded the circumstances and memorialized in full, to the sovereign's intent calling Andu a rebel.
s0264.idiomatic: Jingli recorded everything and memorialized, as the emperor wished, calling Andu a traitor.

s0265.literal: Emperor Wen feared he would not submit to control; in spring of the next year he removed Andu to be Director-General of all military affairs in Jiang and Wu, General Who Campaigns South, and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
s0265.idiomatic: Fearing he would not submit, the next spring the emperor transferred Andu to director-general of all military affairs in Jiang and Wu, general who campaigns south, and Jiangzhou inspector.

s0266.literal: Returning from Jingkou to the capital, his troops entered Shitou; Emperor Wen entertained Andu at Jiade Hall and also gathered his commanders at the Masters of Writing court; at the feast he seized Andu and imprisoned him in the west wing of Jiade, seized his commanders, stripped all horses and arms, and released them.
s0266.idiomatic: Coming from Jingkou his troops entered Shitou; Emperor Wen feasted him at Jiade Hall and assembled his officers at the Masters of Writing court; there he seized Andu and held him in Jiade's west wing, seized his officers, took horses and weapons, and let them go.

s0267.literal: He then produced Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Jingli's memorial to show the court.
s0267.idiomatic: He then produced attendant Cai Jingli's memorial for the court to see.

s0268.literal: An edict then said: "In olden Han they richly rewarded merit-holders, yet Han Xin and Peng Yue raised rebellion; Jin relied on frontier governors, yet Wang Dun and Su Jun took up arms.
s0268.idiomatic: An edict said: "Han richly rewarded its merit-holders, yet Han Xin and Peng Yue rebelled; Jin relied on frontier lords, yet Wang Dun and Su Jun took arms.

s0269.literal: Entrusting a six-foot boy to Pang Meng, treacherous ambition stole forth;
s0269.idiomatic: Entrusting a child to Pang Meng, treachery stirred;

s0270.literal: committing the arms and legs to Huo Yu, wicked designs were secretly framed.
s0270.idiomatic: committing the realm to Huo Yu, conspiracy was secretly laid.

s0271.literal: Looking back at former ages, rebellion follows one pattern; speaking forever of antiquity, disaster shares one rule.
s0271.idiomatic: Looking back, rebellion repeats one pattern; through all antiquity, ruin follows one rule.

s0272.literal: Hou Andu from the first lacked far-reaching design and originally lacked fine virtue; by fortune he met a rising age and took part in state planning, plucked from the ranks and given wings, promoted from a partial commander and entrusted with pursuit.
s0272.idiomatic: Hou Andu never had far sight and lacked virtue from the start; he met a rising age, took part in founding the state, was raised from the ranks and given rank, and as a subordinate commander was trusted with campaigns.

s0273.literal: His rank reached the three Huai trees, his office the four peaks; his titles were lofty and brilliant, his ritual unmatched.
s0273.idiomatic: His rank reached the highest ministers, his post the greatest commands; his honors were dazzling and his ceremony unrivaled.

s0274.literal: Yet his will was only to exalt himself, his spirit bent on lording it over others; he gathered fugitives and exhausted every sort of knavery—unprincipled, without conduct, unafraid and without respect.
s0274.idiomatic: Yet he thought only of himself, his temper overbearing; he gathered fugitives and every sort of knave—lawless, shameless, and insolent.

s0275.literal: Receiving the war tally for sole command, he plundered at will; wherever the chariot hub turned, he extorted without satiety.
s0275.idiomatic: With sole command he plundered at will; in every post he extorted without end.

s0276.literal: Entrusted with Xu and the frontier, bordering Qi territory, he bent to traffic in forbidden goods and sold out the people,
s0276.idiomatic: Posted on the Xu frontier beside Qi, he trafficked in contraband and sold out the people,

s0278.literal: [secretly] burying and digging up [graves], [22] poison flowing through springs and soil, grudge-bearing even against corpses, heedless of law and ritual.
s0278.idiomatic: [secretly] burying loot and digging graves, [22] poison seeping into earth and water, hatred even for the dead, with no regard for law.

s0279.literal: I, at the first founding, because of considerable achievement, flew my carriage to the secondary palace and took part in the good plan; therefore I restrained the offices, always cherishing forbearance, shut out the hundred officials, and daily hoped for self-renewal.
s0279.idiomatic: At the founding I credited his considerable service and his part in the succession plan; I restrained the offices, always hoping he would reform, kept the court from pressing him, and daily looked for renewal.

s0280.literal: I opened my breast in conversation and showed my loyal heart in haste; he rode to his great mansion while the guard stood down, feasted in the high hall while halberds at the steps were unbladed.
s0280.idiomatic: I spoke to him openly and showed trust in haste; he rode to his mansion while the guard stood down, feasted in the high hall while halberds at the steps were sheathed.

s0281.literal: When did I harbor the least suspicion within, dismiss the cypress guard and refuse him lodging, or outwardly feign trust yet on entering the side gate not detain him?
s0281.idiomatic: When did I harbor suspicion within, refuse him lodging, or outwardly feign trust while barring him at the gate?

s0282.literal: Yet he was obstinate and would not repent, arrogant and violent ever more; he enticed civil and military men and secretly harbored alien designs.
s0282.idiomatic: Yet he would not repent and grew ever more violent; he drew in civil and military men and secretly plotted rebellion.

s0283.literal: On the eleventh day of the twelfth month of last year I received Palace Attendant Cai Jingli's memorial saying that on the tenth of last month Hou Andu sent his aide Zhou Hongshi to lodge privately with Jingli, inquiring into the forbidden precinct and fully stating a rebel plan; I still showed forbearance and treated him as before.
s0283.idiomatic: On the eleventh of the twelfth month last year I received attendant Cai Jingli's memorial: on the tenth of last month Hou Andu sent aide Zhou Hongshi to stay privately with Jingli, asking about the inner palace and laying out a plot; I still bore with him and treated him as before.

s0284.literal: From the northern gate he was transferred to southern service; during the interval of receiving orders his treacherous design grew ever clearer.
s0284.idiomatic: From the northern command he was sent south; while taking up the new post his plot grew clearer.

s0285.literal: Now he wished to use his first posting to carry out unrighteous acts.
s0285.idiomatic: Now he meant to use his return to command to carry out treason.

s0286.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be borne?
s0286.idiomatic: If this can be tolerated, what cannot?

s0287.literal: Relying on the altars' spirits, loyal attendants at the bars, his ugly conduct was exposed and his rebellious intent made known.
s0287.idiomatic: Thanks to the state's fortune and loyal attendants at hand, his guilt was exposed and treason revealed.

s0288.literal: Without, let the old statutes be consulted in detail and punishment swiftly set down in the law books; only fellow conspirators [are involved], and nothing further is to be asked.
s0288.idiomatic: Let the statutes be applied and sentence passed swiftly; only fellow conspirators are implicated—no wider inquiry.

s0289.literal: "The next day he was granted death in the west wing; he was forty-four.
s0289.idiomatic: The next day he was granted death in the west wing, aged forty-four.

s0290.literal: Soon an edict pardoned his wife, children, and household; he was buried with the rites of a gentleman, and all funeral needs were to be generously supplied.
s0290.idiomatic: Soon an edict spared his wife, children, and household; he was buried with a gentleman's rites and funeral costs were generously provided.

s0291.literal: Earlier, when the Founder was in the capital, he once feasted with the generals; Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, and Hou Andu offered toasts, each boasting of his achievements.
s0291.idiomatic: Once in the capital the Founder feasted his generals; Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, and Hou Andu toasted, each praising his deeds.

s0292.literal: The Founder said: "You are all fine generals, yet each also has shortcomings."
s0292.idiomatic: The Founder said: "You are all fine generals, yet each has his flaw."

s0293.literal: Master Du is great in aim but dim in judgment, familiar with those below yet arrogant toward superiors, proud of his merit and not gathering in his faults.
s0293.idiomatic: Master Du aims high but sees poorly, is easy with inferiors yet proud toward superiors, and boasts of merit without mending faults.

s0294.literal: Lord Zhou does not choose his associates yet trusts too far, treads danger without setting guards.
s0294.idiomatic: Lord Zhou does not choose friends yet trusts too deeply, faces danger without precaution.

s0295.literal: Lord Hou is frivolous and unrestrained, light and heedless in will.
s0295.idiomatic: Lord Hou is frivolous and unrestrained, light-minded and heedless.

s0296.literal: These are not ways to preserve the whole person."
s0296.idiomatic: None of these is a way to keep oneself whole."

s0297.literal: In the end all were as he said.
s0297.idiomatic: In the end all proved as he had said.

s0298.literal: Andu's eldest son Dun, twelve years old, was Gentleman at the Imperial Secretariat in Extraordinary Capacity; in the second year of Tianjia he fell from a horse and died, posthumously titled Lamented Heir of Guiyang state.
s0298.idiomatic: Andu's eldest son Dun, twelve, was extraordinary gentleman at the imperial secretariat; in Tianjia year 2 he fell from a horse and died, posthumously titled lamented heir of Guiyang state.

s0299.literal: In the third year of Taijian, Emperor Xuan posthumously enfeoffed Andu as Marquis of Chenji county, fief five hundred households, with his son Dan as heir.
s0299.idiomatic: In Taijian year 3 Emperor Xuan posthumously enfeoffed Andu as marquis of Chenji county, fief five hundred households, with son Dan as heir.

s0300.literal: Andu's younger cousin Xiao had repeatedly followed Andu on campaigns with merit, reaching Gentleman at the Imperial Secretariat in Extraordinary Capacity, General of Illustrious Might, Inspector of Eastern Hengzhou, and Marquis of Huaihua county, fief five hundred households.
s0300.idiomatic: Andu's cousin Xiao campaigned with him many times with merit, reaching extraordinary gentleman at the imperial secretariat, general of illustrious might, Eastern Hengzhou inspector, and marquis of Huaihua county with five hundred households.
